title: Variables and built-in functions
game_role: The hero's name, health and gold appear on the game's top bar.
objective: Create variables, get to know data types, read input and use built-in functions
story: Our game is going to have a hero. But how will the computer remember the hero's name, health and gold? Today we open labeled boxes in the computer's memory. We call them **variables**!

sections.title: A variable is a labeled box
sections.body:
A variable is a labeled box you put information into.

```python
name = "Piko"
hp = 100
```

The `=` sign here is not the equals sign from math. It means "put the value on the right into the box on the left". Later you use what's inside by writing the box's name: `print(name)`

sections.title: Naming rules
sections.body:
- Start with a letter or `_`: `score`, `_secret`
- No spaces; use `_` instead: `player_name`
- Upper and lower case are different: `Score` and `score` are separate boxes
- Stick to plain English letters (a–z) in names
- Choose meaningful names: `gold` instead of `x`

sections.title: Data types
sections.body:
You can put different kinds of information into boxes:

- `str` (text): `"Piko"`
- `int` (whole number): `100`
- `float` (decimal number): `3.5`
- `bool` (true/false): `True` or `False`

To find out a value's type, use `type()`: `print(type(100))`

sections.title: Changing what's in the box
sections.body:
Giving a variable a new value replaces the old one:

```python
gold = 10
gold = gold + 5
print(gold)  # 15
```

sections.title: Asking the user
sections.body:
`input()` asks the user for an answer. The answer is **always text** (str). To turn it into a number we use `int()`:

```python
age = int(input("How old are you? "))
```

When the program reaches `input()` it waits for you: type your answer and press Enter.

You can go the other way too: `str(12)` turns a number into text.

sections.title: Python's built-in functions
sections.body:
Python comes with many ready-to-use functions. They are called **built-in functions**. So far you've met `print()`, `input()`, `type()`, `int()` and `str()`. A few more:

- `len("Piko")` gives the length of a text: `4`
- `float("2.5")` turns text into a decimal number
- `round(7.6)` rounds to the nearest whole number: `8`
- `max(3, 9, 4)` gives the largest, `min(3, 9, 4)` the smallest

If you forget what a function does, run `help(len)`.

examples.title: The hero's boxes
examples.code:
name = "Piko"
hp = 100
speed = 2.5
is_alive = True
print(name, hp, speed, is_alive)
print(type(name))
print(type(hp))

examples.title: Update a value
examples.code:
gold = 10
print("At first:", gold)
gold = gold + 25
print("After the treasure:", gold)

examples.title: Let's read input
examples.code:
name = input("What's your name? ")
print("Hello", name)
examples.note: Run it again with a different name.

examples.title: Built-in functions
examples.code:
name = "Piko"
print(len(name))
print(float("2.5") + 1)
print(round(7.6))
print(max(3, 9, 4), min(3, 9, 4))
examples.note: Try to guess each line's result before you run it.

tasks.title: Fill the box
tasks.prompt: Put your own name into the `name` variable and run it.
hints: Only change the name inside the quotes.

tasks.title: Hero card
tasks.prompt: Create three variables: `hero` (the hero's name, text), `age` (their age, a whole number) and `hp` (value 100). Then print all three with `print()`.
tasks.solution:
hero = "Piko"
age = 12
hp = 100
print(hero, age, hp)
hints: Each variable on its own line: hero = ...
age should be a number without quotes: age = 12
To print them all: print(hero, age, hp)

tasks.title: Type detective
tasks.prompt: This code fails because text and a number can't be added together. Turn `a` into a number so that `total` becomes 10. Don't change the line `a = "7"`.
tasks.starter:
a = "7"
b = 3
total = a + b  # This line causes an error!
print(total)
tasks.solution:
a = "7"
b = 3
total = int(a) + b
print(total)
hints: Read the error message: a str can't be added to an int.
int() turns text into a number.

visual_task.title: An army with a variable
visual_task.prompt:
The width of the army is stored in the `width` variable. Print **3 rows**, each with `width` Pikos. Don't count stars by hand: `"*" * width` prints `width` stars side by side.

If you change it to `width = 6`, the army should grow by itself!
visual_task.solution:
width = 4

print("*" * width)
print("*" * width)
print("*" * width)

challenge.title: Swap the boxes
challenge.prompt: You're given two glasses, one with milk and one with juice. To swap them you need a third glass, right? Swap the contents of the variables `a` and `b`. You may not type the words "apple" and "pear" again!
challenge.starter:
a = "apple"
b = "pear"
# swap the contents of a and b

print(a, b)
challenge.solution:
a = "apple"
b = "pear"
temp = a
a = b
b = temp
print(a, b)
hints: Create a third variable: temp = a
Then put b into a, and temp into b.

project_task.title: Player info
project_task.prompt:
Let's keep our hero's info in variables:

- `player_name`: the hero's name
- `player_hp`: 100
- `player_gold`: 0
- `player_level`: 1

Then print a line like `Hero: Piko` (the name should come from the variable).
project_task.solution:
player_name = "Piko"
player_hp = 100
player_gold = 0
player_level = 1
print("Hero:", player_name)
hints: Create the four variables one by one.
